thread.title: Apple (AAPL) Price Target Lowered to $180.00 at Bank of America

author: ABMN Staff
title: Apple (AAPL) Price Target Lowered to $180.00 at Bank of America
text:
Posted by ABMN Staff on Jan 30th, 2019 // No Comments
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) had its price target cut by investment analysts at Bank of America from $190.00 to $180.00 in a research report issued to clients and investors on Wednesday. The firm currently has a “neutral” rating on the iPhone maker’s stock. Bank of America ‘s price target points to a potential upside of 11.53% from the company’s current price.
A number of other research firms have also recently weighed in on AAPL. Nomura restated a “neutral” rating and issued a $185.00 price target on shares of Apple in a report on Monday, November 5th. JPMorgan Chase & Co. set a $228.00 price target on Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a report on Wednesday. Maxim Group restated a “hold” rating and issued a $160.00 price target on shares of Apple in a report on Wednesday. Monness Crespi & Hardt upped their price target on Apple from $200.00 to $220.00 and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a report on Wednesday. Finally, BMO Capital Markets restated a “hold” rating and issued a $153.00 price target on shares of Apple in a report on Wednesday. Three equities research analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, twenty-four have assigned a hold rating and twenty-two have given a buy rating to the stock. Apple presently has a consensus rating of “Hold” and a consensus target price of $193.03. Get Apple alerts:
NASDAQ AAPL traded up $6.71 on Wednesday, hitting $161.39. 16,365,194 shares of the company’s stock were exchanged, compared to its average volume of 34,227,660. The company has a current ratio of 1.12, a quick ratio of 1.09 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.87. Apple has a fifty-two week low of $142.00 and a fifty-two week high of $233.47. The stock has a market capitalization of $768.24 billion, a price-to-earnings ratio of 13.55, a PEG ratio of 1.51 and a beta of 1.23.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its earnings results on Tuesday, January 29th. The iPhone maker reported $4.18 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, topping the Thomson Reuters’ consensus estimate of $4.17 by $0.01. Apple had a return on equity of 48.68% and a net margin of 22.41%. The company had revenue of $84.31 billion for the quarter, compared to analysts’ expectations of $84.07 billion. Equities analysts forecast that Apple will post 11.89 earnings per share for the current fiscal year.
In other Apple news, insider Chris Kondo sold 3,408 shares of the stock in a transaction on Monday, November 19th. The stock was sold at an average price of $190.00, for a total transaction of $647,520.00. Following the transaction, the insider now owns 8,940 shares of the company’s stock, valued at approximately $1,698,600. The sale was disclosed in a filing with the SEC, which is available at the SEC website . Corporate insiders own 0.05% of the company’s stock.
Several institutional investors have recently modified their holdings of the business. Contravisory Investment Management Inc. grew its stake in shares of Apple by 30.6% during the fourth quarter. Contravisory Investment Management Inc. now owns 614 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $97,000 after acquiring an additional 144 shares in the last quarter. Delphi Private Advisors LLC acquired a new stake in shares of Apple during the second quarter valued at about $120,000. Blue Sky Asset Management LLC acquired a new stake in shares of Apple during the second quarter valued at about $108,000. Quattro Financial Advisors LLC acquired a new stake in shares of Apple during the first quarter valued at about $133,000. Finally, Smart Portfolios LLC acquired a new stake in shares of Apple during the first quarter valued at about $134,000. 57.02% of the stock is currently owned by institutional investors.
Apple Company Profile
Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers. It also sells various related software, services, accessories, and third-party digital content and applications. The company offers iPhone, a line of smartphones; iPad, a line of multi-purpose tablets; and Mac, a line of desktop and portable personal computers, as well as iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS operating systems.
